discussions.name: Boulder
discussions.covers: Front Range, Summit County and the northern mountains
messages: Hazardous travel through this evening for the northern mountains and I-70 mountain corridor due to snow and blowing snow. Snowfall amounts greater than 12" likely in the northern tier of mountains.
Potential for snow squalls late this morning to early afternoon with greatest threat in the mountains.
Banded snow (initially mixed with rain) for the the plains and I-25 Corridor today to early this evening. Brief heavy snow but generally light accumulations possible.
Gusty winds in the higher terrain this morning, with gusty winds spreading across the plains this afternoon behind the front.
Return of mostly dry weather Sunday - Tuesday, next system may arrive by Wednesday or Thursday.

discussions.name: Grand Junction
discussions.covers: the western and central mountains, Aspen to the San Juans
messages: Snow is moving in along the northern and central Divide overnight with the heaviest snow falling through the morning and early afternoon. Snow totals of 10-15 inches are expected for the Park and Elkhead mountains, with 4-8 inches across the Flat Tops and Central Divide Mountains.
Winds gusting 40 to 50 mph are expected with this system through Saturday night, leading to blowing and drifting snow and difficult driving conditions over the mountain passes.
An unsettled pattern looks to continue into next week with potential for more mountain snow by mid week, but details remain uncertain.

discussions.name: Pueblo
discussions.covers: the southern mountains: Sangre de Cristos, eastern San Juans, Monarch
messages: Quick moving upper system today, with high winds behind a cold front, snow across the mountains, and brief winter conditions on the Palmer Divide.
Another upper storm system will likely bring precipitation to the region mid week.

report.message:
Happy Thanksgiving! We sure are thankful for colder temps this week as a storm is expected to roll in this weekend.

No new snow to report this morning. For Thanksgiving Eve, we can expect sunny skies with temps in the mid-30s at mid-mountain. Winds will be out of the WNW ranging from 5 to 10 mph and gusting into the 20's.

Yesterday the Pitchfork lift and the Green Acres Beginner Area opened for the season, expanding our early season beginner terrain offerings. We'll have more terrain announcements to share later this week. Keep an eye on our Terrain Updates channel on Instagram to stay locked in with the latest information.

We're now just a few days out from the Stifel Copper Cup, bringing the fastest men in the world to the slopes of East Village. For the full weekend event schedule visit: https://www.coppercolorado.com/copper-cup/event-experience/.

A friendly reminder that early-season conditions are still in play. Ski and ride in control, stay aware of changing surfaces and conditions, and give each other plenty of space. We've got a long season to look forward to still, and we're all in this together.

Happy Turkey Day to those who celebrate!

report.message:
5:22 AM update – Good morning, skiers and riders! Welcome to the Eldora snow report for Saturday, November 28, 2026.

The first Saturday of our winter operating season brings fresh snow: about two inches on the snow stake as of 5:20 AM, with an additional three to five inches throughout the day. Alpenglow chair will spin at 8:30 AM today, serving 1,000 vertical feet of terrain across two top-to-bottom runs, including Hornblower, Windmill, Klondike, and International.

For the full report, please visit Eldora.com/conditions.

report.message:
It's Saturday and a good day to hit the slopes. 35 trails are now open with skiing off 3 lifts, top to bottom, front and back with a 20 inch base of man made and natural snow. Snow showers are possible today but otherwise it will be partly cloudy on the mountain. 

Shuttles are running from the lower parking lots. Equipment rentals are available in the base area and at Purgatory Sports on Main Avenue. 

Skip the lines and get your lift tickets online at store.purgatory.ski, then download your ticket at our kiosks. Hold onto your ticket for the rest of the season and reload it as necessary. Be sure to checkout our lift ticket deals at Purgatory.ski/tickets.


ATTENTION: As we continue to expand our open terrain, please be aware that early season conditions exist. Regardless of a trail being marked as green, all open terrain should be considered intermediate+ with variable early-season conditions.
